html:
Hassan II was the king of Morocco from 1961 to 1999. He made the monarchy the master of Moroccan politics and led the claim to Western Sahara.

He survived two army coup attempts, in 1971 and 1972, and crushed the left-wing opposition. His reign is remembered as the Years of Lead: opponents disappeared, were tortured or held for years in secret prisons such as Tazmamart. In 1975 he launched the Green March into the Spanish Sahara, which rallied Moroccans behind him.

In his last years he opened up, freeing prisoners and letting an opposition party form the government in 1998. He built the Hassan II Mosque in Casablanca. His son Mohammed VI set up a truth commission on the abuses in 2004.
